title: Comorbidities in pediatric patients with severe neurological impairment (SNI) and lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)
summary:
Background

Some children and adolescents have severe damage to the brain or nervous system. This is called a “severe neurological impairment.” These children often develop lower respiratory tract infections, such as pneumonia, and frequently have to be hospitalized. Many of them also have other medical conditions, such as epilepsy, swallowing difficulties, a curved spine, or a heart defect. So far, little is known about which of these conditions cause respiratory infections to take a more severe course.

Research Question

We want to know: Which of these conditions cause children to spend more time in the hospital when they have a respiratory infection? To answer this, we’ll look at how many days the children spent in the hospital and how often they were admitted. We’ll also examine whether they were admitted to the intensive care unit, how long they stayed there, and how long they received supplemental oxygen.

Methodology

We are analyzing data on children and adolescents who were hospitalized between 2016 and 2025 at several large pediatric hospitals in Germany due to a respiratory tract infection. For this study, we are using only data that is already contained in the medical records. No one will undergo new examinations or receive new treatment. We are comparing children with and without the specified conditions and determining whether age, gender, and home ventilation influence the results. We exclude from our calculations children who could only be observed for a short period of time. We also exclude from the intensive care unit analysis children who, for structural or organizational reasons, can only be treated there. We analyze the results in a way that ensures they do not appear unusually striking by chance. The study is a first step toward identifying possible correlations.

interventions.name: Retrospective cohort analysis of pediatric patients with severe neurological impairment (SNI) and lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) 2016–2025

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient treatment lasting at least 24 hours between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2024

Presence of a SNI; defined in accordance with the Delphi consensus-based definition as the presence of all of the following criteria:
o    Permanent central motor impairment (e.g., cerebral palsy)
o    Permanent cognitive impairment (e.g., intellectual disability, speech development delay)
o    Need for support in daily life

Presence of an LRTI, defined here by the presence of at least 3 of the following criteria:
o    Fever (body temperature ≥38.5 °C, measured auricularly)
o    Tachypnea (respiratory rate at least 20% above the age-appropriate normal range)
o    Dyspnea (presence of jugular, intercostal, or subcostal retractions or flaring of the nostrils)
o    Newly developed abnormal pulmonary auscultation findings (as documented in the medical records at admission)
o    Newly developed oxygen requirement of at least 50% above baseline
o    Newly developed pulmonary infiltrate (PI) or parapneumonic effusion (PPE) on a conventional chest X-ray (as documented in a written radiology report by a pediatric radiologist)
Exclusion criteria:
Inadequate data quality due to incomplete, inaccurate, or missing documentation
